statement: The first line holds R and C. The next R lines each hold a string of C digits - an image, one colour digit per pixel. A final line holds sr, sc and newColor. Repaint the region of the starting pixel: every pixel reachable from (sr, sc) through side-sharing pixels of the starting pixel's original colour takes newColor. Print the resulting image, R lines. Guard the do-nothing case: when newColor equals the original colour, the image is unchanged - and a naive walk loops forever.

example.why: The connected 1-region around (1,1) repaints to 2; the 1 at (2,2) touches it only diagonally.

hint: Record the original colour first; the walk tests against it, paints newColor, and moves on.
mistake: Skipping the equal-colours guard - painting 2 over 2 re-queues the same region without end.
